top_story.headline: Veterans Affairs' draft contract for disability exams sets a $40 billion ceiling
top_story.dek: A draft request for proposals posted Friday would split nationwide medical disability examinations among two to four companies per service group.
paragraphs: The Department of Veterans Affairs has posted a draft request for proposals for "Medical Disability Examinations-Next Generation" (solicitation 36C10X27R0001). According to the draft, "The maximum value for MDE-NG is $40,000,000,000 in the aggregate across all MDE-NG IDIQ contracts and all SGs for the entire contract period, including all options." That is a ceiling, not a spending commitment: the same section says the government does not guarantee orders or dollar value above a $3,500,000 minimum.

The draft says the government "intends two to four contracts for each Service Group." The ordering period would be a 12-month base period plus four 12-month option periods. The exams feed the ratings decisions that determine disability compensation and pension benefits. Claimants include veterans and active-duty service members, who can also go through the joint Department of Defense-Department of Veterans Affairs disability evaluation programs.

This comes from a 105-page attachment posted October 9 and read today, on a presolicitation notice from the Veterans Affairs contracting office in Frederick. It is a draft, so terms may change before a final solicitation.

blocks.title: Air Force Research Laboratory wants a hypersonic weapon at under one-fifth the cost and five times the production rate
meta: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Research Laboratory
blocks.text: Late finding, from a call dated October 9 under the lab's broad research solicitation (FA2391-23-S-2403). It says the call will seek "an operationally relevant, air-launched hypersonic weapon for less than 1/5 the cost and greater than 5x the production rate of current systems." A contractor proposing flight testing would have to build at least two flight test vehicles and support at least two flight test events. A separate March call in the same solicitation, for affordable hypersonic weapon concepts, sets aside 15% of base cost as a schedule incentive.

blocks.title: General Services Administration's Washington-area construction contract lets it add contractors and raise the ceiling unilaterally
blocks.text: Late finding, from an agreement document posted September 25 for the D.C. Metro Area multiple-award construction contract. It says the government "reserves the unilateral right to increase the Master Contract MOL by up to 50% of the total aggregate amount" if conditions are met. It can also add contractors at any time and add Virginia and Maryland counties to the coverage area. The document lists work in sensitive secure rooms (SCIFs), high-security data centers and high-security buildings.

blocks.title: Coast Guard's next small response boat must carry machine gun mounts fore and aft
blocks.text: Late finding, from the Response Boat Small Third Generation specification posted September 30. It requires "forward and aft working decks, each accommodating weapon mounts for M240B light machine guns." The camera system must be able to detect "a 30-foot vessel at a range greater than one nautical mile in total darkness."

Bureau of Prisons (Department of Justice) — residential reentry center for 14 Kentucky counties; the statement of work says inmates are eligible for community placement including sex offenders and violent offenders (15BRRC27R00000001; statement of work).

sections.headline: A $35.9 million Army change order for a screwworm fly factory leads a backlog-heavy day
paragraphs: There were 49 new awards of $2 million or more, all 49 Department of Defense awards just published after the 90-day hold, plus 1 large modification and 5 cuts. The 44 routine actions are listed, each linked, in "USAspending: Every Other New Award" at the end of the edition.
Defense items below were signed in July and published this week.

blocks.text: M. A. Mortenson Company received a $35,918,110 change order from the Department of the Army for a new facility to produce 300 million sterile New World screwworm flies per week. It was signed July 10 and published this week; Defense Department contract data is released with a 90-day delay. It is an unusual agricultural pest-control project for the Army (award).

Wawona Frozen Foods Inc had a $6,505,631 contract with the Agricultural Marketing Service (Department of Agriculture) terminated for convenience on October 7. It covered frozen fruit and vegetable commodities for government food donations (award).

Atlas Air, Inc. won $2,443,552 from U.S. Transportation Command for Civil Reserve Air Fleet passenger air transportation labeled "Operation Epic Fury." It was signed July 10 and just made public (award).

Urban Sky Theory Inc received $11,299,090 from the Department of the Air Force for a "Wallabee" micro-balloon intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance system, an unmanned aircraft category. It was signed July 10 and just made public (award).

Coinbase Inc had $6,938,740 removed from its U.S. Marshals Service (Department of Justice) contract for cryptocurrency managed services for seized assets, in a closeout modification on October 7. Closeouts usually return unspent money; the description does not say the work was ended (award).
